messages:
alex: Heads up — noticed a repeating NVMe latency hump in us-west2 last night during the 00:30–01:15UTC window. GPUs couldn't attach for ~2m at a time, provisioning backoff spiked.

maria: saw the same. iostat showed a short 40k IOPS burst on /dev/nvme1n1 and avg rd_lat went from 0.6ms -> 9.8ms. not constant, very spiky. :thinking:

chen: any scrub/cleanup jobs scheduled then?

alex: cron cleaner runs at 00:00 but we usually throttle. logs show cleaner started but there were concurrent checkpoint writes from worker pods.

maria: paste of dmesg snippet from one affected host:

```
[00:31:02] nvme0: I/O 12345 QID 8 timeout, removing
[00:31:03] nvme0n1: write_big: latency 9878us
[00:31:04] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 234567
```

alex: which nodes? I pulled gnode-uw2-102 and gnode-uw2-118. both preemptible.

chen: interesting — both are preemptible. could be degraded wear on cheaper SKUs + concurrent heavy GC. can you check SMART 'percentage_used'?

alex: smartctl output shows "percentage_used": 62% for 102 and 61% for 118. errors are mostly timeout/latency not obvious CRCs.

sam: FYI, we recently bumped ephemeral-cleaner parallelism in that region to speed cleanup during scale-down (cost reason). might be too aggressive.

maria: that matches — cleaner parallelism set to 6 (was 2). spikes line up. suggestion: reduce parallelism to 2 for preemptible pools and add a cool-down between batches.

alex: agree. rolling change idea: patch cleaner config for us-west2 preemptible pool only, reduce parallelism and add 30s jitter. deploy as canary tomorrow midnight.

chen: also propose a temporary routing tweak: route provisioning requests to dedicated pool if io-latency > 5ms for 30s to avoid attach failures. fallback policy exists but not tuned for this threshold.

sam: cost tradeoff acknowledged — short-term extra dedicated spawns may cost ~0.8% of nightly budget but avoid attach retries. good trade.

maria: also adding a metric alert: when nvme_avg_lat_1m > 5ms AND percent_used > 60% on >10% of hosts -> open a pager to oncall, low-priority. helps us notice before provisioning fails.

alex: I'll open a small PR with cleaner change + alert runbook. will also tag the hosts and queue a diagnostic job to capture iostat/smartctl traces during the next window.

sre-bot: deploy-checklist created: PR #4821 (cleaner throttling) -> canary us-west2 preemptible -> monitor 24h -> promote.

sam: thanks — if canary looks good, let's keep the change for 2 weeks then revisit. :thumbsup:
